# Catalog

Every atom and app in one page, small enough to keep loaded whole: what each one is, the ids it mints, and what it needs and offers, by bond kind and declared word ([Bonds](./bonds.md), [Declarations](./declarations.md)). Read this first; open a page only for its rules. The [bond graph](./graph.md) draws the same needs and offers.

53 atoms, 44 with bond lines; 2 app(s).

## Atoms

**[Actor Identity](./atoms/actor-identity.idd)** (817 lines). Actor Identity answers one question: "who authorized this action, and can you prove it?"

- Mints actor id. Offers key actor id.

**[Approval Step](./atoms/approval-step.idd)** (863 lines). Approval Step records a single authorization gate.

- Mints step id. Needs key actor id. Offers key step id.

**[Assignment](./atoms/assignment.idd)** (666 lines). Assignment records who is responsible for a piece of work, and keeps the history of everyone who has held that responsibility.

- Needs key task id; key actor id; journal assignment events.

**[Calendar Time](./atoms/calendar-time.idd)** (927 lines). Calendar Time says what a date and a time of day mean in a place.

- Mints place id. Offers key place id.

**[Capability](./atoms/capability.idd)** (901 lines). Capability is bearer-token authorization: holding a capability's token grants a right, no matter who holds it, and nothing else is asked for to use it.

- Mints capability id. Needs key actor id. Offers key capability id.

**[Capacity Constraint Enforcement](./atoms/capacity-constraint-enforcement.idd)** (1173 lines). Capacity Constraint Enforcement holds one number against another.

- Mints pool id. Needs journal pool events. Offers key pool id.

**[Cart](./atoms/cart.idd)** (723 lines). Cart is a shopping cart: it holds what a person means to buy, one line per item, each line saying how many of the item and the price it had when it was added, and it adds the lines up to a total.

- Mints cart id, line id. Offers key cart id; key line id.

**[Category](./atoms/category.idd)** (805 lines). Category lets a business arrange named categories as a tree — Gardening, and under it Soil and Seeds — and file each item in one home category.

- Mints category id. Needs key opaque. Offers key category id.

**[Comment](./atoms/comment.idd)** (645 lines). Comment lets people answer an item in their own words — a post, a product, a photo — and answer each other, so the comments on an item form a tree of replies.

- Mints comment id. Needs key actor id; key opaque. Offers key comment id.

**[Communication](./atoms/communication.idd)** (792 lines). Communication keeps the history of exchanges between a business and people outside the business: a phone call, an email, a meeting, a message, a letter or a visit.

- Mints communication id. Offers key communication id.

**[Condition Register](./atoms/condition-register.idd)** (801 lines). Condition Register keeps the permanent record of what a background run observed.

- Mints standing id. Offers key standing id.

**[Consent](./atoms/consent.idd)** (875 lines). Consent records a person's agreement to have their personal data used for one named purpose, such as "marketing emails" or "behavioural analytics": when the agreement was given, who collected it, what it covers, and how it ends — the person withdraws it, or it runs out because a time limit was set at grant.

- Mints consent id. Needs key actor id. Offers key consent id.

**[Credential](./atoms/credential.idd)** (978 lines). Credential answers one question: *does this presented material belong to this principal, for this kind of credential?*

- Mints credential id. Needs key actor id. Offers key credential id; follow-up Verify.

**[Duplicate Prevention](./atoms/duplicate-prevention.idd)** (395 lines). Duplicate Prevention gives a system a short-term memory of things it has recently seen, so it can spot repeats.

- No bond lines yet.

**[Durable Intent](./atoms/durable-intent.idd)** (936 lines). Durable Intent is the account a regulated action leaves of something it cannot take back: one record written before the act says what the act is about to do, the adopter's database makes the act, and one record written after says what happened, so that every act has one closing that stands, written by one writer at a time.

- Mints invocation id. Needs guard critical section key; journal closing record, intent record. Offers key invocation id.

**[Erasure Tombstone](./atoms/erasure-tombstone.idd)** (620 lines). Erasure Tombstone keeps the permanent record that one record was destroyed, and under what authority.

- No bond lines yet.

**[Escalation](./atoms/escalation.idd)** (334 lines). Escalation is how a person finishes what the sweep could not: the findings the instance leaves on the deployment's compliance surface (what the sweep could not close and what the instance could not do), the closure-at-risk finding that tells a person an act's window is running out, and [Resolve], the operator's own closing of an act under the same critical section the invocation and the sweep use.

- Needs guard critical section key; key invocation id; journal closing record.

**[Event Log](./atoms/event-log.idd)** (533 lines). Event Log is an append-only record: what is written to it stays in the order it arrived, and by design the log itself never changes or removes it.

- Offers journal.

**[Favorite](./atoms/favorite.idd)** (483 lines). Favorite lets a person mark an item so they can find it again later: a product, a recipe, an article, anything the business shows them.

- Needs key actor id; key opaque.

**[Gift Card](./atoms/gift-card.idd)** (586 lines). Gift Card is a store gift card: a gift card loaded once with a value in one currency, then spent down, in part or in full, until nothing is left.

- No bond lines yet.

**[Invitation](./atoms/invitation.idd)** (891 lines). Invitation tracks the life of an invitation issued to an outside party — a new employee, a customer, a collaborator, a patient — before that party has an identity in the system, and answers *what is the state of this invitation, and who accepted it?*

- Needs key list id; key actor id; journal invitation events. Offers follow-up Accept.

**[Lease](./atoms/lease.idd)** (563 lines). A **lease** lets one worker have a thing to itself until a set time.

- Offers guard opaque.

**[Legal Hold](./atoms/legal-hold.idd)** (776 lines). Legal Hold records a formal instruction to keep one record intact, overriding any normal deletion schedule, until the legal matter behind it ends.

- Mints hold id. Needs key actor id. Offers key hold id.

**[List](./atoms/list.idd)** (447 lines). List holds a name, an author and an id for each list an app makes: make a list, rename it, delete it, read it.

- Mints list id. Needs key actor id. Offers key list id.

**[Medication Order](./atoms/medication-order.idd)** (1438 lines). Medication Order records the whole life of a prescription, from the moment a prescriber places it to its end.

- Mints order id. Needs key actor id; journal order events. Offers key order id.

**[Message Preference](./atoms/message-preference.idd)** (911 lines). Message Preference is an atom — a small, self-contained building block of a larger system — that records how each principal (the person or account the messages are for) wants delivery shaped: which channels, how often at most, what quiet hours, what format.

- Mints preference id. Needs key actor id. Offers key preference id.

**[Moderation](./atoms/moderation.idd)** (630 lines). Moderation lets people flag an item that needs a moderator's eye — a post, a comment, a review — and lets a moderator act on it: hide it or show it again, lock its replies or open them, pin it to the top or unpin it, or dismiss the flags.

- No bond lines yet.

**[Money](./atoms/money.idd)** (785 lines). Money is an amount of money as a value: a whole number of a currency's smallest unit, together with the currency.

- No bond lines yet.

**[Notification](./atoms/notification.idd)** (766 lines). Notification records whether a single piece of information was accepted by the transport for a single recipient.

- Mints notification id. Needs key opaque. Offers key notification id.

**[Observation](./atoms/observation.idd)** (855 lines). Observation records a single measurement about a subject — a vital sign, a lab value, a sensor reading, a financial mark — in a permanent, attributed form that cannot be silently edited.

- Mints observation id. Needs key actor id. Offers key observation id.

**[Ordering](./atoms/ordering.idd)** (450 lines). Ordering keeps the sequence of one list's items: each new item enters at the bottom, one item moves to a new place at a time, and the order reads back, first place to last.

- Needs key opaque; key list id.

**[Owed Record](./atoms/owed-record.idd)** (759 lines). Owed Record keeps the durable record that something is owed.

- No bond lines yet.

**[Party Identity](./atoms/party-identity.idd)** (964 lines). Party Identity is a lasting, verifiable identity record for an external party — a customer, a patient, a counterparty or a beneficial owner (the person who ultimately owns or controls a company).

- Mints party id. Needs key actor id; journal party events. Offers key party id.

**[Permissions](./atoms/permissions.idd)** (661 lines). Permissions answers one question: "is this actor allowed to do this thing right now?"

- Needs key actor id; follow-up Grant. Offers permission opaque.

**[Post](./atoms/post.idd)** (599 lines). Post lets a person write a piece with a title and a body in markdown, keep it as a draft, change it, publish it for readers and take it back down.

- No bond lines yet.

**[Provenance](./atoms/provenance.idd)** (980 lines). Provenance answers one question: who has held this artifact, in what order, from intake to disposition.

- Mints chain id. Needs key actor id. Offers key chain id.

**[Provisional Commitment](./atoms/provisional-commitment.idd)** (811 lines). Provisional Commitment is the business act of holding something for someone while they decide — a card authorization, a hospital bed, an item in a cart, a hotel room, an airline seat.

- Mints commitment id. Needs key actor id; journal commitment events. Offers key commitment id.

**[Punch Card](./atoms/punch-card.idd)** (523 lines). Punch Card is a shop's punch card: a punch card collects one stamp per purchase, and a punch card that has reached its goal, five stamps where the shop sets no other number, is traded for one free item.

- No bond lines yet.

**[Reaction](./atoms/reaction.idd)** (558 lines). Reaction lets a person answer an item with one word from a short list the business offers: "Like" on a post, "Thanks" on an answer, or a small set such as Like, Love and Angry.

- Needs key actor id; key opaque.

**[Recurrence](./atoms/recurrence.idd)** (869 lines). Recurrence says which dates a repeating series falls on.

- Mints series id. Offers key series id.

**[Restorable Delete](./atoms/restorable-delete.idd)** (549 lines). Restorable Delete makes deleting something a two-step act: delete marks an item deleted and opens a window to bring it back, 30 days unless the business sets another; restore brings it back inside that window; purge makes the delete final, and nothing brings back a purged item.

- No bond lines yet.

**[Retention Window](./atoms/retention-window.idd)** (866 lines). Retention Window records each obligation to keep a record for a minimum period, under the retention policy that sets it, and refuses to end that obligation before the period is up.

- Mints retention id. Offers key retention id.

**[Role](./atoms/role.idd)** (641 lines). Role lets a business name sets of allowed actions — member, moderator, admin — and put people in them.

- Mints holding id. Offers key holding id.

**[Selective Disclosure](./atoms/selective-disclosure.idd)** (628 lines). Selective Disclosure keeps a permanent, add-only record of every time someone's data was shared with anyone other than that person — answering the question regulators and individuals routinely ask: what was shared about this person, with whom, under what authority, and when?

- Mints disclosure id. Offers key disclosure id.

**[Session](./atoms/session.idd)** (971 lines). Session answers "is this login still good, and for whom?" without re-checking the password on every request.

- Mints session id. Needs key actor id; key credential id; follow-up Issue. Offers key session id.

**[State Machine](./atoms/state-machine.idd)** (895 lines). State Machine records a single named workflow — think of it as a token moving through a flowchart — where the flowchart (the set of valid states and the transitions between them) is declared by the system deploying it rather than fixed by the pattern itself.

- Mints workflow id. Needs key actor id; journal workflow events. Offers key workflow id.

**[Subscription](./atoms/subscription.idd)** (652 lines). Subscription records who wants to be told about what.

- Mints subscription id. Offers key subscription id.

**[Sweep](./atoms/sweep.idd)** (410 lines). Sweep finishes the account of an act whose invocation died or yielded: a clean-up run, started at every restart and on a set cadence, that looks only at intents whose time limit has passed, takes the same critical section the invocation held, asks the adopter's database whether the act happened, and writes only what it can read back from that database.

- Needs guard critical section key; key invocation id; journal closing record, recovery_intended.

**[Tag](./atoms/tag.idd)** (528 lines). Tag lets a business keep a flat list of named tags — clay, cover-crops, beginners — and put several on one item, so the item is found through any of them.

- Needs key opaque.

**[Tamper Evidence](./atoms/tamper-evidence.idd)** (749 lines). Tamper Evidence answers one question: has this set of records changed since it was sealed?

- Mints evidence id. Offers key evidence id.

**[Task](./atoms/task.idd)** (776 lines). Task keeps the tasks of a list: it records a task in one list, edits it while it is still open, marks it done and saves who did it, and deletes it, or deletes every task of a list when the list ends.

- Mints task id. Needs key list id; key actor id; journal task events. Offers key task id.

**[Tenure](./atoms/tenure.idd)** (768 lines). Tenure records who holds which role in what, and since when: a person, a role such as buyer, billing contact or account manager, the thing the role is held in — a customer, a deal, a club — a start date, and an end date once the tenure ends.

- Mints tenure id. Offers key tenure id.

**[Waitlist](./atoms/waitlist.idd)** (785 lines). Waitlist keeps people in line, first come, first served, for something with no room left: a full class, an earlier appointment, a sold-out item waiting on returns.

- Mints spot id, waitlist id. Offers key waitlist id; key spot id.

## Apps

**[Recoverable Invocation as an app](./apps/recoverable-invocation/index.md)**. Atoms: Durable Intent, Escalation, Event Log, Lease, Sweep.

- Durable Intent needs guard critical section key: met by Lease.
- Durable Intent needs journal closing record, intent record: met by Event Log.
- Escalation needs guard critical section key: met by Lease.
- Escalation needs key invocation id: met by Durable Intent.
- Escalation needs journal closing record: met by Event Log.
- Sweep needs guard critical section key: met by Lease.
- Sweep needs key invocation id: met by Durable Intent.
- Sweep needs journal closing record, recovery_intended: met by Event Log.

**[Shared Todo as an app](./apps/todo/index.md)**. Atoms: Actor Identity, Assignment, Credential, Event Log, Invitation, List, Ordering, Permissions, Session, Task.

- Assignment needs key task id: met by Task.
- Assignment needs key actor id: met by Actor Identity.
- Assignment needs journal assignment events: met by Event Log.
- Credential needs key actor id: met by Actor Identity.
- Invitation needs key list id: met by List.
- Invitation needs key actor id: met by Actor Identity.
- Invitation needs journal invitation events: met by Event Log.
- List needs key actor id: met by Actor Identity.
- Ordering needs key opaque: met by Actor Identity, Credential, List, Session, Task.
- Ordering needs key list id: met by List.
- Permissions needs key actor id: met by Actor Identity.
- Permissions needs follow-up Grant: met by Invitation.
- Session needs key actor id: met by Actor Identity.
- Session needs key credential id: met by Credential.
- Session needs follow-up Issue: met by Credential.
- Task needs key list id: met by List.
- Task needs key actor id: met by Actor Identity.
- Task needs journal task events: met by Event Log.
- Shared Todo as an app needs permission actor id: met by Permissions.
